text:
anna: Quick sync — we need to lock semantics for org-wide API keys vs project-scoped tokens before the PRD hits review. Customer asks: should billing and ownership be tied to the org key or the project token? Also need clear revocation and rotation rules. @mike @sara

mike: TL;DR: org keys = admin/service-level, not for embedding; project tokens = least-privilege, bill to project. For PRD we should state: ownership, billing attribution, revocation semantics, TTL/refresh model, and migration story. Launch criteria should include a beta customer using project tokens. :white_check_mark:

anna: Can you sketch the acceptance criteria we want in the PRD? I can paste into the doc.

mike: Acceptance criteria (draft):
- API: endpoints accept both org_key and project_token with consistent auth header. Example: `Authorization: Bearer proj_<id>.<sig>` or `Authorization: Bearer org_<id>.<sig>`.
- Billing: requests authenticated with project_token attribute usage to the project; org_key attributes to org.
- Revocation: revoking a project token immediately invalidates it across all services (propagated within 30s).
- Rotation: support key rotation without downtime (support old key grace period configurable, default 1h).
- Audit: all token issue/rotate/revoke events logged and queryable in console for 90d.
- UX: console flow to create project tokens with explicit scopes and TTL.
- Security: project tokens disallow admin-only operations by default.
- Backcompat: existing org keys continue to work for GA, but we discourage embedding them in client apps.

sara: Implementation notes from infra:
- We'll implement token type in JWT claims: `typ=org|project`, `scope=[...]`, `proj_id` (optional).
- Service-side check: `if typ==project then enforce project membership and scope checks` (done in middleware).
- We need a global revocation table (Redis + pubsub) for immediate invalidation. If not found, fallback to token verification time window.
- Edge case: what happens when a project is deleted? Proposed: cascade revoke all project tokens and keep audit events.

jess: From customers: mobile apps prefer short-lived tokens (15m) + refresh token. For server-to-server, long-lived project tokens (30d) are common. Need guidance in PRD. Also some customers want a "service" project token that multiple teams share — must call out recommended patterns and risks.

anna: Good point. Add migration path: existing org keys -> recommended to create project tokens and update integrations; provide a bulk-mint tool + rollout checklist for customers.

mike: Edge cases to call out in PRD:
- Token created for a project user who later leaves org: should token remain valid? My proposal: tokens are independent of user after creation (they're bearer tokens). If tied to user, revoke on user removal; if service token, remain unless revoked. PRD should require explicit "created_as_service" flag.
- Cross-project access: forbid by default. Admin org keys can set cross-project ACLs.
- Rate limits: quota attribution by token; org-wide quotas still apply for org_keys.
- Partial failover: if revocation pubsub partitioned, stale tokens may remain valid for up to X seconds — document SLA and mitigation.

anna: Quick UX acceptance items: console create token flow, CLI `redwood tokens create --project X --scopes read,generate --ttl 30d --service`, docs page, migration guide, and a beta toggle in org settings.

auth-bot: Note: deploy plan requires `feature_flag.tokens_scoped` enabled in prod for rollout; scheduled rollout window requested.

mike: Owners / next steps:
- PRD: anna to own drafting (deadline Wed EOD).
- Infra design + revocation: sara + eng-infra to produce design doc (Thu).
- Security review & threat model: eng-security to review (Fri).
- Beta outreach: jess to run with customer success.

anna: I'll add the acceptance criteria list to the PRD and ping for review. Thanks — let's keep scope minimal for v1: issue/create/revoke/rotate + audit + console flow. We can follow up on refresh-token flows in v1.1. :rocket:
